one_sentence_story: Claude Steele and Joshua Aronson proved in 1995 that reminding committed students of an unfair stereotype right before a hard GRE test hijacks scarce working memory with anxious self-monitoring — dragging scores down unless reframed or moved to the end of the test.
so_what_for_you: Remove stereotype landmines before high-stakes performance: put demographic questions at the END of forms, frame tough stretches as learnable mechanics rather than fixed 'worth,' and pair high standards with clear belief in someone's capability.
